question.problem:
Consider the boundary value problem

$$
{y}^{″}+9y=f(x),\,y(0)=0,\,y(1)=4
$$

where $f(x)$ is $2$-periodic and even. Select the missing part in the solution of the BVP, where the infinite sum on the right-hand side below represents a particular solution ${y}_{p}$ of the differential equation.

*Hint: In this specific problem, the forcing function $f(x)$ is chosen such that the particular solution ${y}_{p}$ satisfies ${y}_{p}(0)=0$ and ${y}_{p}(1)=0.$*

$$
y(x)∼{{field-1}}+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x).
$$
question.worked_solution:
We write the solution as $y={y}_{c}+{y}_{p}$, where ${y}_{c}$ solves the homogeneous equation and ${y}_{p}$ is a particular solution.

First, solve the homogeneous equation ${y}^{″}+9y=0.$ Its general solution is

$$
{y}_{c}(x)=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).
$$

Now, we use the hint. Since ${y}_{p}(0)=0$ and ${y}_{p}(1)=0$, we have

$$
y(0)={y}_{c}(0)\,\text{and}\,y(1)={y}_{c}(1).
$$

Next, we apply the boundary conditions.

- Use $y(0)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) & =A\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+{y}_{p}(0) \\ 0 & =A(1)+B(0)+0 \\ A & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, ${y}_{c}(x)=B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).$

- Use $y(1)=4$ with $A=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(1) & =B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3)+{y}_{p}(1) \\ 4 & =B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3)+0 \\ B & =\frac{4}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
y(x)∼\frac{4}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3)}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x).
$$
